brief: Binds {name} placeholders in a document's texts to values, so setting a value changes the screen without rebuilding it.
detail: A placeholder is an ordinary string with braces in it, so the document format is unchanged. Set gives a name a value and re-renders only the elements that mention it; SetMany does several at once and updates each affected element once; Apply pushes everything. The document survives an update, so there is no re-parse, no new font registration and no rebuilt accessibility tree, and focus and hover stay where they were. Text changes still re-shape the whole document, style changes through SetStyle are surgical. The class substitutes text and sets style properties and computes no meanings. Layout needs the engine and a font, no window.
receiver:
oDoc = new stzUiDocument('DEFINE PANEL console ( SIZE [400, 200], DIRECTION column, PADDING 10, CHILDREN [title, readout] ) RATIONALE "A console."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE TEXT title ( CONTENT "NAV - {mode}", SIZE 20 ) RATIONALE "The mode."' + char(10) + 'DEFINE TEXT readout ( CONTENT "BEARING {bearing} RANGE {range} km", SIZE 16 ) RATIONALE "The numbers."')
oDoc.UseFont("C:/Windows/Fonts/segoeui.ttf")
oPanel = oDoc.ToPanel()
o1 = new stzUiBindings(oDoc, oPanel)
